decisionsTitle: «Schimbă adresa»: an Administrator moves a registration to another address (reversing «no verified-email edit» and §645's locked address)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-11-11:** «aparent nu pot modifica mailul unei persoane???». Told that the address cannot be changed by the team, on purpose — the address is the person's identity, their links and their declaration go to it, and the written rule says «the address stays the person's» — and offered three answers (only the addresses the person never confirmed, the recommended one; leave the rule as it is; any address, at any time, not recommended), he chose **«Orice adresă, oricând»**: the Administrator may change any address, a confirmed one included.

**Decision — this REVERSES «no verified-email edit» (`DECISIONS.md` §33, §67, BR-REQ-037-03 criterion 2) and «Modifică datele»'s locked address (§645), on the owner's instruction.** A new Administrator-only verb, «Schimbă adresa», on the registration's own card «Adresa de email» (beside «Datele înscrierii», never inside it): one registration per press, in any state, at any time.

1. **The data move.** `participants.canonical_email` stays the immutable identity (`AGENTS.md` §10.4): no participant row is ever rewritten or merged. The registration is re-pointed — `registrations.participant_id` set to the participant of the new canonical address, reused exactly as it is (its name and language untouched; `findOrCreateParticipant`, which refreshes both on an unverified row, is not used) or created, unverified, with the registration's name and language. Under the event's lock, in one transaction, the row read again under it (`service.ts#changeRegistrationAddressByStaff`). The state, the place, the waiting position and the race number do not move; the allocator is asked nothing. Two nullable columns record it, `address_changed_at` and `address_changed_by_staff_user_id` (migration `0198`); the vouching columns stay the old address's facts.
2. **The links.** Every live action link of the registration is revoked for cause (`invalidated_at`, no `superseded_by_token_id`), so an old link gets the one generic refusal and never «a newer email exists». And every registration-scoped token is **bound** to the registration's current participant, at read and at spend (`action-tokens/repository.ts`): a link whose participant is not the registration's is a missing token — whatever else is true of it (superseded, spent, expired), so the old address learns nothing of where the registration stands.
3. **The mail.** The old address's participant messages for the row still waiting and never tried are withdrawn with their club copies, and the renderer withdraws a retry or a claimed one (`render.ts`, `OutboxMessageWithdrawn`): no link is ever minted for the old address. The club's archive and notice keep their own rules.
4. **What each address is told.** Two new message types, neither carrying a token (migration `0197`, an `ADD VALUE` of its own): `REGISTRATION_ADDRESS_REMOVED` to the old address — the organizers changed the address of «name»'s registration at the event, its links no longer work, and the contact page if this was not asked for; never the new address; queued whatever that address's refusals say — and `REGISTRATION_ADDRESS_ADDED` to the new address — it now receives the registration's emails, where the registration stands, whether the next step follows, the contact page if it is not theirs. The body is the part the club may reword; the dead links, the status and the contact page are the platform's lines after it. Then the state's own message to the new address: the verification with the club's email-link window again from the move, the waiting-list message, the offer, the declaration, or the confirmation with a **new check-in code**, so the QR the old address holds opens nothing.
5. **The trail.** One audit row, `registration.address_changed_by_staff`, on the old participant, the registration as its entity, with ids, counts and flags only — never an address — scrubbed of the two participant ids by the erase and the retention sweep. A declaration signed afterwards from an emailed link is shown on the registration's page as «semnată din linkul trimis la adresa schimbată de echipă» (`domain/address-change.ts#signedAfterStaffAddressChange`), and a timeline line says when and by whom the address was changed.
6. **The person's record.** «Toate datele unei persoane» shows each address only its own mail: the new address sees the registration and its trail, never the mail sent to the old one; the old address sees its own messages, the notice and the move's row by its participant. Erasing either address acts on its own rows.

**Safeguards that keep every other rule true.** No participant merge and no rewritten participant row (§10.4). Nothing vouched and nothing signed in the same press: the declaration is still the person's, from the new address's own link, so «no staff-signed declaration» stays checkable — the trail shows the signature as given after a staff address change, never as staff's. The allocator is not touched (no place moves, nobody passes anybody). The old links die twice over — revoked, and refused by the binding. The old address is always told, with no token and without the new address. «Oferte și beneficii» is a consent: withdrawn. Refused, writing nothing, each said at the box: an address that is not one (`ADDRESS_INVALID`); the same address, a provider's variant included (its canonical form or its inbox, `ANSWERS_UNCHANGED`); the same runner already on the new address at the event, active or not, or at another event of the race while this one is active (`STAFF_ALREADY_ON_ADDRESS`); the new address at the club's limit per address, or the schema's one per address (`STAFF_ADDRESS_AT_CAP`); a family form waiting on the row (`ADDRESS_FAMILY_FORM_PENDING`); an open invitation of the new address to the event, which the moved row would adopt (`ADDRESS_INVITED`); an erased registration (`NOT_FOUND`). A unique violation the checks did not foresee is answered as `ALREADY_ON_ADDRESS`, never raw. The Administrator's alone (`canManageRegistrations`), asserted by the action, the wrapper and the service; the Organizer reads the address and gets no form. The family left on the old address with a step still to take is sent the family's own message again, to the old address. The orphan sweep keeps an old participant while its notice of the move is still to leave. Under real concurrency (`tests/concurrency/address-change.test.ts`): two moves onto one address at a limit of one, exactly one succeeds; a move racing a public form of the same runner, one wins and nothing raw reaches the screen — the lock every entry takes before it reads an address serializes them.

**Decided for the owner (the three questions the design left open):**
1. **A hold's or an offer's deadline** is kept; when less than 24 hours remain it becomes 24 hours from the change, capped by the event's start — but for a counted place **never while anybody is eligible on the waiting list**: lengthening a counted hold then would keep a place ahead of the person waiting beyond what the allocator's own deadline gives them (`AGENTS.md` §10.5–§10.6), so the deadline is kept as it was. A place «Pe lista de invitați speciali» takes no counted place and may be lengthened. A deadline already passed, or none, is left to the allocator's own rules.
2. **A cancelled or lapsed registration, or one after the event has ended** (cancelled, completed, or past its end, its start without one), may be moved: rectification still matters. It gets the two notices alone — no link, no step.
3. **«Vreau să primesc oferte și beneficii»** is withdrawn by the move, audited exactly as staff's withdrawal is (`registration.promo_consent_changed`, `via: STAFF`, on the old address's trail): the consent was given from the old address, and the question before the press says so when the person had given it.

**For the lawyer.** No legal text or template is changed. The declaration's «din linkul trimis pe adresa de email confirmată» is met as it is by an address the club vouched for (§637, §872). What is new: a declaration may now be signed from a link sent to an address the club set after the person's own; the page shows such a signature as «semnată din linkul trimis la adresa schimbată de echipă», and the trail says who changed the address and when. Whether the club's texts should say that the organizers may correct a wrong address on request (the privacy notice's «Rectificare: corectăm datele greșite» already covers it) is the club's to word at its next revision.

**Refused inside the verb.** Changing the address and vouching or signing in one press («Dă-i un loc acum» stays a press of its own); a silent change (the two notices are not optional); changing an erased registration; the new address in the old notice or in the trail; merging participant rows, or rewriting `participants.delivery_email`, which every registration on that address shares; moving a whole family in one press (one registration per press); leaving the old links alive (both the revoke and the binding are required); offering the verb to the Organizer or at the desk.
changelogLine: - **«Schimbă adresa»** — an Administrator can now change a registration's email address, on its own card «Adresa de email»: the registration moves to the new address with its place, state and number, every link sent to the old address stops working, both addresses get an email about the change, the new one gets the next step (a confirmed runner a new QR code), and the consent to offers and benefits is withdrawn. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends the status line and criterion 2. Given the backoffice, when it renders, then it offers no participant merge and rewrites no participant row; an address is changed only by «Schimbă adresa», which re-points one registration to the participant of the new canonical address (2026-11-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 19. Given a registration's page, then the Administrator — and nobody else — is offered «Schimbă adresa» on the card «Adresa de email», the Organizer reading the address with no form; and the words on the rejected-email line and in «Ce îi spui» say to ask for the right address, which an administrator changes in «Adresa de email», never that only the person can, by registering again (2026-11-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an Administrator moving a registration in any of its seven states to another address, when it commits, then under the event lock and in one transaction `participant_id` is the new canonical address's participant — reused unchanged or created, no participant row rewritten or merged — with `address_changed_at` and `address_changed_by_staff_user_id`; the state, the place, the waiting position and the race number are unchanged; every live link of the registration is revoked for cause; the old address's queued participant mail for it is withdrawn; `REGISTRATION_ADDRESS_REMOVED` (no token, no new address, the contact page) is queued to the old address despite any open refusal, `REGISTRATION_ADDRESS_ADDED` to the new one, then the state's own message — the verification with a fresh window, the waiting list, the offer, the declaration, or the confirmation with a new check-in code — none for a cancelled or lapsed row or an event that is over; a hold or offer under a day from its end gets a day from the move, capped by the start, only while nobody waits; «oferte și beneficii» is withdrawn and audited; the old address's family with a step to take is sent its message again; one audit row holds ids and counts and no address, scrubbed by the erase; a declaration signed afterwards from an emailed link is shown as signed after a staff address change (2026-11-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given «Schimbă adresa», when the address is not valid, is the same address or a provider's variant of it, already holds this runner at the event (active or not) or at another event of the race, is at the club's limit per address, or has an open invitation to the event, or a family form waits on the row, or the row was erased, then it is refused with its own sentence at the box and nothing is written, and two moves or a move and a public form racing for one address never reach the database's unique index as a raw failure (2026-11-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a registration-scoped action token whose participant is not the registration's current one, when it is read or spent for any purpose, then it is answered exactly as a missing token — never «a newer email exists», «already used» or «expired» — and the renderer withdraws a participant message queued for a registration whose participant changed since, the old address's notice of the move excepted (2026-11-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given «Schimbă adresa», when each of the seven roles presses it, then only the Administrator and the Superadministrator move the registration; every other role is refused FORBIDDEN by the action and, with its gate standing aside, by the service, and nothing is written (2026-11-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a registration moved to another address, when «Toate datele unei persoane» is read for either address, then the new address shows the registration and none of the mail sent to the old one, and the old address shows its own messages, the notice of the move and the move's audit row, never the new address's mail; and the orphan sweep keeps the old participant while its notice of the move is still to leave (2026-11-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: «Schimbă adresa»: an Administrator moves a registration to another address, old links dead, both addresses told
